tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Pre-registration: is `conventions --module` retrievable? (#418)

Written 2026-10-28, BEFORE any candidate derivation was drawn or scored. Edits after
that date go in a dated addendum, never over this text.

## Question

Given a structural question an agent actually asked itself while working, does
`compute_module_view` (CLI `conventions --module`, MCP `archy_module_view`) return the
answer, complete and correct? This is coverage of the lookup, not whether an agent
reaches for it: six delivery-line interventions have already come back null, so no agent
time is spent here.

## Unit and sampling

The unit is a DERIVATION: one assistant text or thinking block from an archived
transcript that states or asks a structural fact about the code under work.

- Source: `bench/q1b_transcripts` and `bench/greenfield_transcripts` only. The original
  24 (development data) came from the archy footprint corpus, so
  `bench/agent_footprint_transcripts` is excluded.
- Candidates: blocks matching the keyword filter in `bench/retrievability_draw.py`
  (imports, imported by, consumers of, reach, depends on, import cycle). The filter is
  fixed before reading any candidate.
- Draw: seeded random sample (seed 418) of candidates, stratified by corpus, labelled in
  draw order. Stop at 40 derivations that the labeller marks `structural` (below), or
  when candidates run out, whichever is first. Derivations are not cherry-picked after the
  draw; a candidate is skipped only for the reasons in the label table.

## Labels (assigned from the question text alone, BEFORE running the view)

| label | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `direct` | answerable from one module's direct imports or importers |
| `transitive` | needs "reaches" across more than one hop, or "any of A reaches B" |
| `docs` | about documentation or non-code content |
| `tests` | about test helpers or test modules |
| `other` | not a structural import question (behavior, values, runtime); excluded from the denominator |

`structural` = `direct` + `transitive`. Labelling `transitive` requires quoting the
phrase that needs more than one hop.

## Scoring

For each `structural` derivation, the labeller works out the ground truth by grep on
the tree the transcript ran against, then records the expected answer. The view is run on
that tree. A derivation scores:

- **answered** if the view's output contains the answer, complete (a negative needs the
  target absent from a list the view marks as complete);
- **not answered** otherwise, including `transitive` ones, which `ModuleView` cannot
  state in one call. Reported separately so the gap is visible.
- Runs on a tree that cannot be reproduced at the transcript's commit are DROPPED, never
  counted as answered.

Baseline arm: the same questions scored against the ordinary `conventions` report (top 12
default). Pilot: the first 5 structural derivations are scored against both arms before
the thresholds below are applied, to confirm the baseline is not saturated (the #369
trap). If the baseline answers 4 or 5 of the 5, the contrast is uninformative and the
result is reported as such, with no claim made.
"""Duplicate-function detection via AST-shape hashing (advisory, not a score axis).

Clusters functions whose *normalized* body shape is identical: identifiers and
literals are folded to placeholders before hashing (see
`archy.complexity._analyze_body`), so two functions that differ only by names or
literal values land in the same cluster. A minimum `size` (normalized AST-node
count) threshold skips trivial getters and stubs, whose shapes collide but are
not duplication in the refactor-this sense.

This is a same-shape cluster *surfacer*, not a precision oracle. Output is split
into two tiers by a semantic de-noiser (`classify_variants`): a primary "likely
duplicate" tier (investigate these) and a demoted "variant" tier of
likely-intentional clusters (same-class siblings, `@overload` stubs, trivial
boilerplate, and path-isolated copies - clusters wholly in test suites or
vendoring/isolation dirs, issue #247). Nothing is hidden; the variant tier is
down-ranked, not dropped.
Within the primary tier, `exact` marks byte-identical (Type-1) clusters: the
concrete (un-normalized) body hashes match, so these are real copy-paste, the
highest-confidence slice (~63% precision on a 12-repo re-validation, ~74% on
non-test source, vs ~50% for the tier overall; §12d).

Refactorability is a *semantic* judgment that syntax cannot fully make. The clone
literature is blunt about this: Kapser & Godfrey found up to 71% of real clones
are benign (parameterized "templating" siblings, boilerplate, per-backend
variants), so ~50% refactorability precision is the expected ceiling for any
similarity-only detector, and no production tool (SourcererCC, NiCad, Deckard)
solves the benign-vs-refactorable split - they measure Type-1/2/3 similarity, a
different question. The one non-ML signal that measurably breaks the ceiling is
change-history co-change (a cluster whose members co-change consistently is
refactorable; one that never co-changes is benign, ~94% precision in the
literature). `demote_independent` consumes it (issue #242, via the
change-coupling machinery from #131): a primary cluster whose copies live in
actively-maintained files that never co-change is demoted to the `variant` tier
(reason `"independent"`), lifting primary precision above the syntactic ceiling.
The calling agent remains the final semantic judge. See
`docs/research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §12c/§12f.

All of the above is exact AST-shape hashing, which finds only Type-1/2 clones; a
single inserted/reordered statement moves the hash (measured ~0% Type-3 recall,
§12g). `compute_near_duplicates` (issue #246) adds an opt-in, lower-confidence
`"near_miss"` tier for Type-3 (gapped) recall: a graded token-multiset overlap
(`extract_token_bags`, the same folding hashed as a *set* not a sequence) that a
small edit barely perturbs. See §12h.

Never folded into `archy score`. Even at ~50% it beats dead-code detection, which
the same FP discipline rejected outright at ~100% FP.

Unlike module-grained diagnostics (`hotspots`, `dsm`) that read the shared
`nx.DiGraph`, this one is function-grained: the graph keeps only per-module CC
aggregates, so `compute_duplicates` consumes the `(modules, parse_results)` pair
from `archy.graph.parse_project` instead.

archy:owns        DuplicateGroup, DuplicateMember, classify_variants,
                  compute_duplicates, compute_near_duplicates, demote_independent,
                  is_test_path
archy:mirrored-by DuplicateGroup -> archy.cli_render_git, archy.mcp_payloads,
                  archy.mcp_runs_git, classify_variants -> archy.cli_git,
                  archy.mcp_runs_git, bench.duplicates_cochange_sweep,
                  compute_duplicates -> archy.cli_git, archy.mcp_runs_git,
                  bench.duplicates_cochange_sweep,
                  compute_near_duplicates -> archy.cli_git, archy.mcp_runs_git,
                  bench.near_duplicates_sweep, demote_independent -> archy.cli_git,
                  archy.mcp_runs_git, bench.duplicates_cochange_sweep,
                  is_test_path -> archy.cli_git, archy.mcp_runs_graph,
                  bench.coupling_sweep, bench.duplicates_cochange_sweep,
                  bench.reach_asymmetry_precision
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from collections import Counter
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from itertools import combinations
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from archy.complexity import (
    FunctionComplexity,
    FunctionFeatures,
    extract_function_features,
    extract_token_bags,
)
from archy.graph import Module
from archy.parser import ParseResult

_V = TypeVar("_V")

# 30 is the calibrated shipping default: the FP spot-check (RESEARCH_METRICS.md
# section 12) showed the trivial-boilerplate false positives (property shims,
# one-line delegations) cluster below ~30 normalized nodes, while dropping the
# floor lower floods the list and raising it much higher starts losing genuine
# small duplicates. The floor removes only the trivial tail; the two-tier
# de-noiser (classify_variants) handles the structural intentional-clone classes,
# and co-change history (#131) is the semantic precision layer beyond that.
DEFAULT_MIN_SIZE = 30
DEFAULT_MIN_MEMBERS = 2

# Change-coupling demotion thresholds (issue #242), calibrated on the bench.
# A primary cluster whose copies live in >=2 actively-maintained files that
# never co-change is deliberately independent (per-backend siblings, symmetric
# methods) -> demote. `min_evidence` is the guard against demoting a real but
# rarely-touched duplicate: absence of co-change is only meaningful when both
# files change often enough to have HAD the chance to move together.
DEFAULT_COCHANGE_MIN_SUPPORT = 3
DEFAULT_COCHANGE_MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.3
DEFAULT_COCHANGE_MIN_EVIDENCE = 5

# Type-3 near-miss thresholds (issue #246), calibrated on the bench (§12h). The
# exact shape-hash catches Type-1/2 but nothing gapped; the token-multiset overlap
# below finds Type-3 clones (a small edit changes the bag only slightly). The
# similarity floor is high (0.85) because the normalized-token vocabulary is tiny,
# so a loose threshold collides unrelated same-shaped functions; the spot-check
# put the FP tail there in coincidental trivial-method (dunder) matches, with the
# top-ranked clusters (async/sync twins, parallel validators) genuine.
DEFAULT_MIN_SIMILARITY = 0.85
# Global cap on pairwise token comparisons in the near-miss pass, the safety
# valve against a size-band with thousands of same-sized functions on a giant
# repo. If hit, the pass warns (never silently truncates) and returns what it
# found within budget.
DEFAULT_MAX_NEAR_COMPARISONS = 5_000_000


def compute_duplicates(
    modules: list[Module],
    parse_results: dict[str, ParseResult],
    *,
    min_size: int = DEFAULT_MIN_SIZE,
    min_members: int = DEFAULT_MIN_MEMBERS,
) -> list[DuplicateGroup]:
    """Cluster functions by normalized body shape across all modules.

    Buckets every function whose `size >= min_size` by its `shape_hash`, keeps
    buckets with at least `min_members` members, and returns them ranked by
    `(-redundancy, -size, -member_count, shape_hash)`. Clustering is by
    `shape_hash` alone; the 128-bit blake2b digest makes accidental collision
    negligible, so a composite key is unnecessary.

    Raises `ValueError` for `min_members < 2` (a group of one is not a
    duplicate); the invariant lives here so every caller inherits it, not just
    the CLI.
    """
    if min_members < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"min_members must be >= 2; got {min_members}")
    buckets: dict[str, list[DuplicateMember]] = {}
    size_by_hash: dict[str, int] = {}
    for qual, path, fn in _sized_functions(modules, parse_results, min_size):
        buckets.setdefault(fn.shape_hash, []).append(_member(qual, path, fn))
        size_by_hash[fn.shape_hash] = fn.size

    groups: list[DuplicateGroup] = []
    for shape_hash, members in buckets.items():
        if len(members) < min_members:
            continue
        ordered = tuple(sorted(members, key=_member_sort_key))
        size = size_by_hash[shape_hash]
        groups.append(
            DuplicateGroup(
                shape_hash=shape_hash,
                size=size,
                member_count=len(ordered),
                redundancy=size * (len(ordered) - 1),
                members=ordered,
                same_class=_same_class(ordered),
            )
        )
    groups.sort(key=lambda g: (-g.redundancy, -g.size, -g.member_count, g.shape_hash))
    return groups


def compute_near_duplicates(
    modules: list[Module],
    parse_results: dict[str, ParseResult],
    *,
    min_size: int = DEFAULT_MIN_SIZE,
    min_similarity: float = DEFAULT_MIN_SIMILARITY,
    max_comparisons: int = DEFAULT_MAX_NEAR_COMPARISONS,
) -> list[DuplicateGroup]:
    """Type-3 (gapped) clone clusters via token-multiset overlap (issue #246).

    The exact `shape_hash` finds Type-1/2 clones but nothing gapped (one inserted
    statement moves the hash; §12g measured ~0% Type-3 recall). This pass
    compares the normalized-token *multiset* (`extract_token_bags`, the same
    folding `shape_hash` hashes as a sequence) with a graded `min_similarity`
    threshold, which a small edit barely perturbs. Returns `category="near_miss"`
    groups carrying a `similarity` (the component's weakest edge).

    Only functions with `size >= min_size` whose `shape_hash` is a **singleton**
    (fewer than 2 occurrences) are candidates: a Type-3 pair are both singletons,
    and this keeps the near-miss tier disjoint from the exact/near tiers. Because
    Jaccard `>= t` forces the two sizes within a factor `1/t`, candidates are
    sorted by size and each is compared only forward while the size stays in
    band - the cheap prefilter that avoids the O(n^2) blow-up the tiny token
    vocabulary would otherwise cause (no rare tokens to index on). A global
    `max_comparisons` budget bounds giant repos; exceeding it warns rather than
    silently truncating.
    """
    sized = list(_sized_functions(modules, parse_results, min_size))
    items = _near_miss_candidates(sized)
    components, edge_weight = _cluster_by_similarity(items, min_similarity, max_comparisons)

    groups = [
        _near_miss_group(items, members_idx, edge_weight, min_similarity)
        for members_idx in components.values()
        if len(members_idx) >= DEFAULT_MIN_MEMBERS
    ]
    groups.sort(key=lambda g: (-(g.similarity or 0.0), -g.redundancy, -g.size))
    return groups

- Candidates: blocks matching the keyword filter in `bench/retrievability_draw.py`
  (imports, imported by, consumers of, reach, depends on, import cycle). The filter is
  fixed before reading any candidate.
- Draw: seeded random sample (seed 418) of candidates, stratified by corpus, labelled in
  draw order. Stop at 40 derivations that the labeller marks `structural` (below), or
  when candidates run out, whichever is first. Derivations are not cherry-picked after the
  draw; a candidate is skipped only for the reasons in the label table.

## Labels (assigned from the question text alone, BEFORE running the view)

| label | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `direct` | answerable from one module's direct imports or importers |
| `transitive` | needs "reaches" across more than one hop, or "any of A reaches B" |
| `docs` | about documentation or non-code content |
| `tests` | about test helpers or test modules |
| `other` | not a structural import question (behavior, values, runtime); excluded from the denominator |

`structural` = `direct` + `transitive`. Labelling `transitive` requires quoting the
phrase that needs more than one hop.

## Scoring

For each `structural` derivation, the labeller works out the ground truth by grep on
the tree the transcript ran against, then records the expected answer. The view is run on
that tree. A derivation scores:

- **answered** if the view's output contains the answer, complete (a negative needs the
  target absent from a list the view marks as complete);
- **not answered** otherwise, including `transitive` ones, which `ModuleView` cannot
  state in one call. Reported separately so the gap is visible.
- Runs on a tree that cannot be reproduced at the transcript's commit are DROPPED, never
  counted as answered.

Baseline arm: the same questions scored against the ordinary `conventions` report (top 12
default). Pilot: the first 5 structural derivations are scored against both arms before
the thresholds below are applied, to confirm the baseline is not saturated (the #369
trap). If the baseline answers 4 or 5 of the 5, the contrast is uninformative and the
result is reported as such, with no claim made.
"""Duplicate-function detection via AST-shape hashing (advisory, not a score axis).

Clusters functions whose *normalized* body shape is identical: identifiers and
literals are folded to placeholders before hashing (see
`archy.complexity._analyze_body`), so two functions that differ only by names or
literal values land in the same cluster. A minimum `size` (normalized AST-node
count) threshold skips trivial getters and stubs, whose shapes collide but are
not duplication in the refactor-this sense.

This is a same-shape cluster *surfacer*, not a precision oracle. Output is split
into two tiers by a semantic de-noiser (`classify_variants`): a primary "likely
duplicate" tier (investigate these) and a demoted "variant" tier of
likely-intentional clusters (same-class siblings, `@overload` stubs, trivial
boilerplate, and path-isolated copies - clusters wholly in test suites or
vendoring/isolation dirs, issue #247). Nothing is hidden; the variant tier is
down-ranked, not dropped.
Within the primary tier, `exact` marks byte-identical (Type-1) clusters: the
concrete (un-normalized) body hashes match, so these are real copy-paste, the
highest-confidence slice (~63% precision on a 12-repo re-validation, ~74% on
non-test source, vs ~50% for the tier overall; §12d).

Refactorability is a *semantic* judgment that syntax cannot fully make. The clone
literature is blunt about this: Kapser & Godfrey found up to 71% of real clones
are benign (parameterized "templating" siblings, boilerplate, per-backend
variants), so ~50% refactorability precision is the expected ceiling for any
similarity-only detector, and no production tool (SourcererCC, NiCad, Deckard)
solves the benign-vs-refactorable split - they measure Type-1/2/3 similarity, a
different question. The one non-ML signal that measurably breaks the ceiling is
change-history co-change (a cluster whose members co-change consistently is
refactorable; one that never co-changes is benign, ~94% precision in the
literature). `demote_independent` consumes it (issue #242, via the
change-coupling machinery from #131): a primary cluster whose copies live in
actively-maintained files that never co-change is demoted to the `variant` tier
(reason `"independent"`), lifting primary precision above the syntactic ceiling.
The calling agent remains the final semantic judge. See
`docs/research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §12c/§12f.

All of the above is exact AST-shape hashing, which finds only Type-1/2 clones; a
single inserted/reordered statement moves the hash (measured ~0% Type-3 recall,
§12g). `compute_near_duplicates` (issue #246) adds an opt-in, lower-confidence
`"near_miss"` tier for Type-3 (gapped) recall: a graded token-multiset overlap
(`extract_token_bags`, the same folding hashed as a *set* not a sequence) that a
small edit barely perturbs. See §12h.

Never folded into `archy score`. Even at ~50% it beats dead-code detection, which
the same FP discipline rejected outright at ~100% FP.

Unlike module-grained diagnostics (`hotspots`, `dsm`) that read the shared
`nx.DiGraph`, this one is function-grained: the graph keeps only per-module CC
aggregates, so `compute_duplicates` consumes the `(modules, parse_results)` pair
from `archy.graph.parse_project` instead.

_V = TypeVar("_V")

# 30 is the calibrated shipping default: the FP spot-check (RESEARCH_METRICS.md
# section 12) showed the trivial-boilerplate false positives (property shims,
# one-line delegations) cluster below ~30 normalized nodes, while dropping the
# floor lower floods the list and raising it much higher starts losing genuine
# small duplicates. The floor removes only the trivial tail; the two-tier
# de-noiser (classify_variants) handles the structural intentional-clone classes,
# and co-change history (#131) is the semantic precision layer beyond that.
DEFAULT_MIN_SIZE = 30
DEFAULT_MIN_MEMBERS = 2

# Change-coupling demotion thresholds (issue #242), calibrated on the bench.
# A primary cluster whose copies live in >=2 actively-maintained files that
# never co-change is deliberately independent (per-backend siblings, symmetric
# methods) -> demote. `min_evidence` is the guard against demoting a real but
# rarely-touched duplicate: absence of co-change is only meaningful when both
# files change often enough to have HAD the chance to move together.
DEFAULT_COCHANGE_MIN_SUPPORT = 3
DEFAULT_COCHANGE_MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.3
DEFAULT_COCHANGE_MIN_EVIDENCE = 5

# Type-3 near-miss thresholds (issue #246), calibrated on the bench (§12h). The
# exact shape-hash catches Type-1/2 but nothing gapped; the token-multiset overlap
# below finds Type-3 clones (a small edit changes the bag only slightly). The
# similarity floor is high (0.85) because the normalized-token vocabulary is tiny,
# so a loose threshold collides unrelated same-shaped functions; the spot-check
# put the FP tail there in coincidental trivial-method (dunder) matches, with the
# top-ranked clusters (async/sync twins, parallel validators) genuine.
DEFAULT_MIN_SIMILARITY = 0.85
# Global cap on pairwise token comparisons in the near-miss pass, the safety
# valve against a size-band with thousands of same-sized functions on a giant
# repo. If hit, the pass warns (never silently truncates) and returns what it
# found within budget.
DEFAULT_MAX_NEAR_COMPARISONS = 5_000_000


def compute_duplicates(
    modules: list[Module],
    parse_results: dict[str, ParseResult],
    *,
    min_size: int = DEFAULT_MIN_SIZE,
    min_members: int = DEFAULT_MIN_MEMBERS,
) -> list[DuplicateGroup]:
    """Cluster functions by normalized body shape across all modules.

    Buckets every function whose `size >= min_size` by its `shape_hash`, keeps
    buckets with at least `min_members` members, and returns them ranked by
    `(-redundancy, -size, -member_count, shape_hash)`. Clustering is by
    `shape_hash` alone; the 128-bit blake2b digest makes accidental collision
    negligible, so a composite key is unnecessary.

    Raises `ValueError` for `min_members < 2` (a group of one is not a
    duplicate); the invariant lives here so every caller inherits it, not just
    the CLI.
    """
    if min_members < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"min_members must be >= 2; got {min_members}")
    buckets: dict[str, list[DuplicateMember]] = {}
    size_by_hash: dict[str, int] = {}
    for qual, path, fn in _sized_functions(modules, parse_results, min_size):
        buckets.setdefault(fn.shape_hash, []).append(_member(qual, path, fn))
        size_by_hash[fn.shape_hash] = fn.size

    groups: list[DuplicateGroup] = []
    for shape_hash, members in buckets.items():
        if len(members) < min_members:
            continue
        ordered = tuple(sorted(members, key=_member_sort_key))
        size = size_by_hash[shape_hash]
        groups.append(
            DuplicateGroup(
                shape_hash=shape_hash,
                size=size,
                member_count=len(ordered),
                redundancy=size * (len(ordered) - 1),
                members=ordered,
                same_class=_same_class(ordered),
            )
        )
    groups.sort(key=lambda g: (-g.redundancy, -g.size, -g.member_count, g.shape_hash))
    return groups


def compute_near_duplicates(
    modules: list[Module],
    parse_results: dict[str, ParseResult],
    *,
    min_size: int = DEFAULT_MIN_SIZE,
    min_similarity: float = DEFAULT_MIN_SIMILARITY,
    max_comparisons: int = DEFAULT_MAX_NEAR_COMPARISONS,
) -> list[DuplicateGroup]:
    """Type-3 (gapped) clone clusters via token-multiset overlap (issue #246).

    The exact `shape_hash` finds Type-1/2 clones but nothing gapped (one inserted
    statement moves the hash; §12g measured ~0% Type-3 recall). This pass
    compares the normalized-token *multiset* (`extract_token_bags`, the same
    folding `shape_hash` hashes as a sequence) with a graded `min_similarity`
    threshold, which a small edit barely perturbs. Returns `category="near_miss"`
    groups carrying a `similarity` (the component's weakest edge).

    Only functions with `size >= min_size` whose `shape_hash` is a **singleton**
    (fewer than 2 occurrences) are candidates: a Type-3 pair are both singletons,
    and this keeps the near-miss tier disjoint from the exact/near tiers. Because
    Jaccard `>= t` forces the two sizes within a factor `1/t`, candidates are
    sorted by size and each is compared only forward while the size stays in
    band - the cheap prefilter that avoids the O(n^2) blow-up the tiny token
    vocabulary would otherwise cause (no rare tokens to index on). A global
    `max_comparisons` budget bounds giant repos; exceeding it warns rather than
    silently truncating.
    """
    sized = list(_sized_functions(modules, parse_results, min_size))
    items = _near_miss_candidates(sized)
    components, edge_weight = _cluster_by_similarity(items, min_similarity, max_comparisons)

    groups = [
        _near_miss_group(items, members_idx, edge_weight, min_similarity)
        for members_idx in components.values()
        if len(members_idx) >= DEFAULT_MIN_MEMBERS
    ]
    groups.sort(key=lambda g: (-(g.similarity or 0.0), -g.redundancy, -g.size))
    return groups

"fmt",
    type=click.Choice(["text", "json"]),
    default="text",
    help="Output format.",
)
def duplicates(
    path: Path,
    min_nodes: int,
    top_n: int,
    min_members: int,
    co_change: bool,
    near_miss: bool,
    fmt: str,
) -> None:
    """Surface clusters of functions with identical normalized body shape.

    Folds identifiers and literals to placeholders, hashes the body's AST shape,
    and clusters matches (see `archy.duplicates`). Output is two tiers: "likely
    duplicate(s)" to investigate, and demoted "variant(s)" that are likely
    intentional (same-class siblings, boilerplate, test/vendored copies, and -
    with `--co-change`, the default when git is present - copies whose files are
    actively maintained yet never change together, i.e. deliberately independent
    implementations). `--near-miss` adds a lower-confidence Type-3 tier: gapped
    clones (a copy with statements inserted/removed) that the exact shape-hash
    cannot see, found by token-multiset overlap. Advisory only (never changes
    `archy score`); a cluster means "investigate," not "provably identical."
    Refactorability is a semantic call, so the ~50% precision ceiling is left to
    the reader's judgment. Trivial functions below `--min-nodes` are skipped.
    """
    # Validate before any parse work so bad flags fail fast and consistently.
    _require(min_nodes >= 1, "min-nodes", ">= 1", min_nodes)
    _require(top_n >= 1, "top", ">= 1", top_n)
    _require(min_members >= 2, "members", ">= 2", min_members)
    try:
        modules, parse_results = parse_project(
            path, **_graph_kwargs_or_exit(path), max_modules=resolve_max_modules(path)
        )
    except ScanTooLargeError as exc:
        raise click.ClickException(str(exc)) from exc
    rows = classify_variants(
        compute_duplicates(modules, parse_results, min_size=min_nodes, min_members=min_members)
    )
    if co_change:
        # git-backed precision layer (#242): demote clusters whose copies never
        # co-change. Best-effort - a non-git tree simply leaves the tiers as-is.
        cochange = git_cochange(path, keep_paths=frozenset(str(m.path) for m in modules))
        if cochange is not None:
            rows = demote_independent(
                rows, counts=cochange.counts, pair_support=cochange.pair_support
            )
    if near_miss:
        # Type-3 recall layer (#246): opt-in token-overlap pass over the
        # singletons the exact hash missed, appended as `near_miss` groups the
        # renderers show in their own lower-confidence section.
        rows = rows + compute_near_duplicates(modules, parse_results, min_size=min_nodes)
    if fmt == "json":
        payload = _duplicates_to_dict(rows, top_n=top_n, min_nodes=min_nodes)
        click.echo(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    else:
        click.echo(_duplicates_to_text(rows, top_n=top_n, min_nodes=min_nodes))

# Pre-registration: does a diff-scoped "re-implemented an existing function" finding fire often enough, and is it right when it fires? (#548)

Written 2026-11-11, BEFORE `bench/diff_duplicates_precision.py` exists, before any PR was
drawn, and before any label was read. Edits after this date go in a dated addendum at the
bottom, never over this text. The commit that adds this file is quoted in the results.

## Question

`archy duplicates` reports the duplication backlog of a whole tree. A reviewer asks a
narrower thing at change time: did this diff add a function that already exists elsewhere?
Keeping only the clusters with one member inside the diff's added lines and one member that
already existed at the base commit would turn the report into that check. This study measures
two numbers on Python agent PRs before anything is built:

1. **Firing rate:** how many PRs produce at least one such cluster.
2. **Precision:** of the firings, how many are cases where the new function should have
   called or reused the existing one.

It measures the clones archy can see (AST-shape exact plus token-overlap near-miss). It does
not claim to cover Type-4 (semantic) redundancy, which is the kind the agent-PR literature
measures (arXiv 2601.21276) and which this detector misses by design. Low recall is expected
and is not a finding of this study.

No agent time is spent. The unit of work is a git checkout and a parse, so the expensive part
of any bench here (live agent runs) does not apply.

## The action, if it passes

The PR author or the agent is told "new `f` in `a/x.py` matches existing `b/y.f`" and deletes
the copy in favour of a call. If the study fails, nothing is built and
`docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md` records why. This ticket ships no CLI flag, MCP parameter or hook,
is never a score input, and adds no embeddings and no per-turn hook output.

## Prior art recorded before the run

- **SonarQube Cloud, "Sonar way for agentic AI"** already fails a PR whose new code has more
  than 3% duplicated lines. A Python duplicated block there needs at least 100 successive
  duplicated tokens over at least 10 lines, with only indentation and string literals
  ignored, so a copy with renamed identifiers is not a duplicate to Sonar. archy folds
  identifiers and literals. The gate is a density threshold, so one 15-line copy in a
  600-line PR (2.5%) passes. See "Reported, never decisive" for what this study records
  about it.
- **mick-gsk/drift** ships the in-loop version as a Claude Code hook and measures its own
  speak-rate by replay (0.0% to 5.6% on five repos). Its first run said 27% to 69% and the
  output was junk; the classes it derived are enumerated below so they are counted as
  reasons for FALSE labels instead of tuned away after the fact. Its replay measures noise,
  not precision or effect, so it does not change the anti-theater answer for this ticket.
- Detector precision history: about 50% similarity-only ceiling, about 63% exact tier, about
  74% source with co-change demotion (#242, #247, `docs/LEARNINGS.md`). Co-change abstains
  for files with fewer than 5 commits (`min_evidence`), so a copy in a NEW file falls back
  toward the ceiling. This study is expected to land nearer 50% than 74% for that reason.
- Two shipped detectors missed their pre-registered precision bars: Study 7 (0.024 against
  0.70) and Study 9 (0.215 against 0.40). Both harness bugs in Study 7 produced
  publishable-looking numbers, which is why the canary below runs before any real run.

## Population and sampling

- **Source:** AIDev (`hao-li/AIDev`), tables `pull_request` (state, `merged_at`, `repo_url`,
  `agent`) and `pr_commit_details` (`filename`, `status`, `patch`, per commit). The base
  commit and head commit of each PR are recovered from the repository's git history, not
  from the dataset.
- **Python PR:** a PR with at least one `.py` file whose patch carries an added line. Merged
  and closed-unmerged PRs are both in; open PRs are out (no outcome and the head moves).
- **Pilot:** 20 Python PRs drawn with seed 548. The pilot is disjoint from the main sample
  by construction (drawn first, removed from the pool).
- **Main sample:** N Python PRs drawn uniformly at random from the remaining pool with seed
  548 and at most 25 PRs per repository (the cap stops one prolific repository from
  supplying the whole firing set; it is applied in draw order). N is fixed in the
  post-pilot addendum from the pilot's measured wall time per PR, and only from that. The
  sample is not extended after the run starts: a short result is a result.
- **Unmeasurable PRs are dropped, never scored clean.** A PR whose base or head cannot be
  checked out, whose tree fails to parse, or whose scan exceeds the module cap is recorded
  with its reason and removed from the denominator. Dropped counts are reported by reason,
  and the headroom rate is also reported with every dropped PR counted as a non-firing, so
  the effect of dropping is visible.

## The detector and what counts as a firing

The shipped detector, unmodified, run on the head tree:

- exact clusters: `compute_duplicates(min_size=30)`, then `classify_variants`, then
  `demote_independent` where git history is present (the `archy duplicates` default);
- near-miss clusters: `compute_near_duplicates(min_size=30)` at the shipped 0.85 floor.
  These have no variant tier of their own, so the harness applies the same path filter
  (below) to them;
- **source-only (#247):** a cluster is dropped if any member is a test path
  (`is_test_path`) or a vendored path. Exact clusters the detector demotes to the `variant`
  tier are dropped. No other filter is added.

A cluster is a **firing** iff both hold, computed from `git diff base..head`:

- **A (new):** at least one member's `def` line falls inside an added hunk of the diff;
- **B (pre-existing):** at least one OTHER member existed at base, in a location outside the
  added hunks (a function present at base whose lines the diff did not add).

One firing is one (PR, cluster) pair. The unit of precision is the firing. Firings in one PR
are reported both ways (per firing and per PR) so a single PR cannot hide behind a count.
Only clusters the diff touches can fire, so a backlog cluster wholly at base never counts.

Headroom is `PRs with at least one firing / measured Python PRs`.

## Oracles

### Primary: blind labels from two labelers under the frozen rubric

Each scorable firing is labelled by two labelers working independently. Each sees the
repository, the new function and the existing function (paths, bodies, surrounding file),
and is blind to: the detector tier and similarity, the PR's merge outcome, the reviewers'
comments, and the git oracle. They label each firing TRUE or FALSE, and for FALSE record one
reason from the list below.

**TRUE** means: the new function should have called or reused the existing one (directly,
or by extracting a shared helper both call).

**FALSE** means: the duplication is intended or benign.

Frozen rubric for FALSE, one reason recorded per firing:

| reason | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sibling` | per-backend, per-provider, per-version or per-format siblings that differ in ways the shape folds away |
| `boilerplate` | property shims, one-line delegation, dunder methods, argument-parsing scaffolds, CLI or schema glue |
| `example-or-test-like` | examples, docs, scripts, fixtures, migrations or generated code restating a name by design (including paths the harness did not recognise as test or vendored) |
| `isolation` | deliberate independence: vendored or forked code, a layer that must not import the other |
| `same-class` | symmetric methods of one class or one protocol |
| `widespread-name` | the same shape appears in many places as a convention, so no single "existing one" exists to reuse |
| `short-or-trivial` | too small for reuse to be worth a call, despite clearing 30 nodes |
| `other` | free text, which the labeller must write |

A firing is **TRUE under the primary oracle only if both labelers say TRUE.** A split
decision is FALSE for the headline. The lenient reading (either says TRUE) is reported as
the upper bound and the strict reading as the headline; if they straddle a threshold, the
strict one decides. Cohen's kappa is reported with the counts. Labelers are recorded by
identity in the results; the labelling script reads nothing but the rubric and the two
functions.

If the firing set exceeds 120, a seeded draw (seed 548) of 120 is labelled, before anything
else is read. Below that, every firing is labelled.

**Firings that cannot be scored are dropped, never scored as clean.** A firing is
unscorable if either labeller cannot open the pre-existing member at its location, or the
two functions cannot be located at head. Drops are reported by reason.

### Secondary, reported and never decisive: the git oracle

A firing scores TRUE if the copy was removed or consolidated in a later revision of the same
PR or within 6 months on the default branch: the new function's qualified name is gone, or
its body no longer shares a shape with the existing member. The oracle is biased against the
feature, since reviewers do not object to redundant agent code (2601.21276), so it can only
under-count. It never decides a threshold.

### Reported, never decisive: the Sonar comparison

For each firing the primary oracle scores TRUE, record:

1. whether the copy is at least 10 lines and identifier-identical (byte-identical concrete
   body, which is the `exact` tier);
2. the PR's new-code duplicated-line density from the same added hunks. This is a PROXY:
   duplicated lines are the added lines of functions that are members of kept clusters, over
   all added lines in `.py` files. It is not Sonar's 100-token, 10-line detector and is
   labelled as a proxy wherever it appears.

If almost every TRUE firing would also have failed Sonar's 3% gate, the results say so,
because a follow-up feature would then add nothing for SonarQube users. The slice archy
alone would add is short copies, renamed copies, near-misses and copies diluted below 3% by
a large PR; any follow-up has to justify that slice. This adds no threshold.

## Thresholds

Fixed here, and not moved by the pilot or by anything read afterwards.

- **Headroom kill:** fewer than 1 firing per 50 Python agent PRs in the main sample (a rate
  below 2%), OR fewer than 30 scorable firings from at least 10 repositories. Either means
  the feature is not built. This is a result, not "underpowered, try again."
- **Precision pass:** at least 0.60 over at least 30 scorable firings from at least 10
  repositories, under the primary oracle.
- **Precision kill:** below 0.40.
- **Between 0.40 and 0.60:** null, and not shipped.

**No post-hoc subgroup rescues a null.** Exact versus near-miss, and new file versus
existing file, are reported in full, with counts and the reason breakdown, but they are not
results. The detector is not edited after the first labelled firing: the FALSE reasons above
are what a filter would have to remove, and removing them after seeing the labels would be
tuning on the test set.

## Process, in order

1. This document is committed. Its hash goes in the results.
2. The harness, the added-hunk unit tests (hand-built two-commit fixture; red when "member
   existed at base" is removed, red again when "def line inside an added hunk" is removed;
   the fixture asserts it contains a pre-existing match before asserting the outcome) and
   the canary.
3. `--canary`: a fixture PR that copies an existing function into a NEW file must fire, and a
   fixture PR that only edits an existing function must not. It runs before any real run.
4. Pilot on 20 disjoint PRs. **No labels are read.** It reports firing rate and harness bugs.
   A pilot of 20 expects well under one firing at a 2% rate, so it cannot estimate the rate
   and is a plumbing test only; the addendum says so. Its one design output is N, from
   wall time per PR.
5. Dated addendum fixing N, then the full run, resumable from the ledger (one row per PR,
   appended in a single write, only `status="ok"` counts as done, a crash in one PR does not
   end the run, stalls are retried and results never).
6. Labelling, then scoring against the thresholds, then
   `bench/diff_duplicates_precision_results.md` and a Study entry in
   `docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md`, published pass or fail.

## Descriptive extra, not a threshold

The headroom measurement already yields a speak-rate comparable to drift's replay numbers;
it is reported next to them so a reader can see whether archy would be noisier than the
in-loop tool that exists today.

## Addenda

None yet.

**STOP and redirect** if either of these applies:

- User wants to **configure, create, or modify** review rules (e.g., "add a security review", "set up reviews for our API layer") → use the `configure_reviews` skill instead
- User wants to **add a doc-sync rule** (keep a documentation file in sync with source files) → call `start_workflow` with `job_name="deepwork_reviews"` and `workflow_name="add_document_update_rule"`

Only proceed past this section if the user wants to **run** reviews.

## Pre-flight — Verify Agent Availability

Before running reviews, check that the `deepwork:reviewer` agent is available. If it does not appear in the agents list (i.e., the Agent tool does not list `deepwork:reviewer` as a valid `subagent_type`), **STOP** and tell the user:

> The `deepwork:reviewer` agent is not available. Please run `/reload-plugins` to pick up the latest plugin updates, then try again.

Do not proceed with reviews until the agent is available.

## How to Run

1. Call the `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions` tool directly:
   - **No arguments** to review the current branch's changes (auto-detects via git diff against the main branch).
   - **With `files`** to review only specific files: `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions(files=["src/app.py", "src/lib.py"])`. When provided, only reviews whose include/exclude patterns match the given files will be returned. Use this when the user asks to review a particular file or set of files rather than the whole branch.
   - **If the result says no rules are configured**: Ask the user if they'd like to auto-discover and set up rules. If yes, invoke the `/deepwork` skill with the `deepwork_reviews` job's `discover_rules` workflow. Stop here — do not proceed with running reviews if there are no rules.
2. The output will list review tasks to invoke in parallel. Each task has `description`, `subagent_type`, and `prompt` fields — these map directly to the Agent tool parameters. Launch all of them as parallel agents.
3. **While review agents run**, check for a changelog and open PR (see below).
4. Collect the results from all review agents.

## Changelog & PR Description Check

Run this concurrently with the review agents (step 2 above) — don't wait for reviews to finish first.

1. Check if the project has a changelog file (e.g., `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGELOG`, `CHANGES.md`).
2. If a changelog exists and there are commits on the current branch beyond the main branch:
   - Read the changelog and the branch's commit log (`git log main..HEAD --oneline`).
   - Verify the changelog's unreleased/current section accurately reflects what the branch does. If entries are missing, outdated, or inaccurate, update the changelog.
3. If a PR is open for the current branch (check with `gh pr view`):
   - If you updated the changelog, also verify the PR description matches. Update it with `gh pr edit` if needed.
   - If the changelog was already accurate, skip the PR description check.

## Acting on Results

For each finding from the review agents:

- **Obviously good changes with no downsides** (e.g., fixing a typo, removing an unused import, adding a missing null check): make the change immediately without asking. When in doubt, ask.
- **Everything else** (refactors, style changes, architectural suggestions, anything with trade-offs):
  1. Use AskUserQuestion to ask the user about each finding **individually**. Do not group issues together unless they are the same issue occurring in multiple files; otherwise, use AskUserQuestion to ask about each issue separately. This lets the user make separate decisions on each item.
  2. For each question, provide several concrete fix approaches as options when there are reasonable alternatives (e.g., "Update the spec to match the code" vs "Update the code to match the spec" vs "Skip").
  3. If a finding seems minor or debatable, include an option to suppress that error in the future — such as a clarification to the rule if it is too narrow, or a comment on the offending content if comments work in that context.
  4. Be concise — quote the key finding, don't dump the full review.

When a finding is dismissed (user chooses "Skip" or you determine it's not actionable for this PR), call `mcp__deepwork__mark_review_as_passed` with the review's ID so it won't re-run on subsequent iterations.

## Iterate

After making any changes:

1. Call `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions` with `files` set to **only the files you edited** during this iteration. This scopes the re-review to your changes rather than re-reviewing the entire branch.
2. Repeat the cycle (run → act on results → run again) until a clean run — one where all review agents return no findings, or all remaining findings have been explicitly skipped by the user.
3. On subsequent runs, you only need to re-run tasks that had findings last time — skip tasks that were clean.
4. Reviews that already passed are automatically skipped as long as reviewed files remain unchanged.

"""Supervised subprocess execution and resumable ledgers for the agent benches.

Extracted from the pain of #282 and #289, where a single bench run is hours of
live agent time and two failure modes made that expensive:

1. **Headless `claude` stalls.** Observed in #282: a run alive for 19 minutes
   having consumed 2 seconds of CPU. `bench/agent_footprint.py` calls
   `subprocess.run` with no timeout, so a stalled run hangs until a human
   notices and kills it.
2. **No resume.** Records append to `records.jsonl` as they complete, so
   finished work survives a crash, but nothing reads that back. Re-running
   after a failure re-does every completed run at full agent cost.

## What "stalled" means here, precisely

A stall is **not** "taking a long time". A model generating a long response, or
a test suite running for eight minutes, are both healthy and must not be
killed. The distinguishing property of the #282 pathology is that the process
was doing *nothing*: no output, no file writes, no CPU.

So a run is declared stalled when, for `stall_after` seconds continuously:

- **no watched path advanced its mtime** (the agent's transcript directory and
  the repo working tree, so any streamed token or any file edit counts as
  progress), **and**
- **the child consumed less than `cpu_epsilon` seconds of CPU** over that same
  window.

Both conditions are required. Either alone produces false kills: a long quiet
`Bash` tool call can leave mtimes untouched while CPU burns, and a process
blocked on a slow network read can tick a log file while using no CPU.

## Why CPU comes from `ps` and not from stdlib

"""Supervised subprocess execution and resumable ledgers for the agent benches.

Extracted from the pain of #282 and #289, where a single bench run is hours of
live agent time and two failure modes made that expensive:

1. **Headless `claude` stalls.** Observed in #282: a run alive for 19 minutes
   having consumed 2 seconds of CPU. `bench/agent_footprint.py` calls
   `subprocess.run` with no timeout, so a stalled run hangs until a human
   notices and kills it.
2. **No resume.** Records append to `records.jsonl` as they complete, so
   finished work survives a crash, but nothing reads that back. Re-running
   after a failure re-does every completed run at full agent cost.

## What "stalled" means here, precisely

A stall is **not** "taking a long time". A model generating a long response, or
a test suite running for eight minutes, are both healthy and must not be
killed. The distinguishing property of the #282 pathology is that the process
was doing *nothing*: no output, no file writes, no CPU.

So a run is declared stalled when, for `stall_after` seconds continuously:

- **no watched path advanced its mtime** (the agent's transcript directory and
  the repo working tree, so any streamed token or any file edit counts as
  progress), **and**
- **the child consumed less than `cpu_epsilon` seconds of CPU** over that same
  window.

blocked on a slow network read can tick a log file while using no CPU.

for this. It only accounts for children that have already been **reaped**, so a

every live process, which is precisely when it is needed.

that I/O will ever complete, which is not visible in the syscall and is only
observable as absence of progress over time.

"""Shared helpers for the bench sweep scripts.

Extracted so `hotspots_sweep.py` and `duplicates_sweep.py` (and any future
sweep) share one manifest loader and one clone/checkout routine instead of
copy-pasting them. Sweep scripts are run as `python bench/<name>.py`, so
`bench/` is on `sys.path[0]` and this module imports as `from _common import ...`.

archy:owns        clone_or_update, load_manifest
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import yaml  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
MANIFEST = REPO_ROOT / "bench" / "projects.yaml"
WORKDIR = Path("/tmp/archy_bench")


def load_manifest() -> list[dict]:
    return yaml.safe_load(MANIFEST.read_text())["projects"]


def _has_commit(target: Path, sha: str) -> bool:
    probe = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(target), "cat-file", "-e", sha], capture_output=True, check=False
    )
    return probe.returncode == 0


def clone_or_update(proj: dict) -> Path | None:
    """Clone/checkout a project at its pinned SHA; never raises -- on any failure
    return None so the caller can skip the project and keep the sweep going. The
    archy self-entry uses REPO_ROOT directly (its pin may name a tag that does
    not exist yet during a release PR)."""
    name = proj["name"]
    sha = proj["sha"]
    if name == "archy":
        return REPO_ROOT
    target = WORKDIR / name
    if not target.exists():
        WORKDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        res = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", "--quiet", f"https://github.com/{proj['repo']}.git", str(target)],
        )
        if res.returncode != 0:
            return None
    if not _has_commit(target, sha):
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(target), "fetch", "--quiet", "origin"], check=False)
    # A shallow clone cannot resolve an abbreviated pin, and a plain fetch does not
    # deepen it, so the checkout below failed and the project was skipped with no
    # reason given (found piloting #870, against clones cached shallow).
    if not _has_commit(target, sha):
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(target), "fetch", "--quiet", "--unshallow", "origin"],
            capture_output=True,
            check=False,
        )
    if (
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(target), "checkout", "--quiet", sha],
        ).returncode
        != 0
    ):
        return None
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(target), "reset", "--hard", "--quiet", sha], check=False)
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(target), "clean", "-fdx", "--quiet"], check=False)
    return target

from archy.duplicates import (
    classify_variants,
    compute_duplicates,
    demote_independent,
    is_test_path,
)
from archy.graph import parse_project

RESULTS = REPO_ROOT / "bench" / "duplicates_cochange_results.md"


def run_project(root: Path) -> dict | None:
    try:
        modules, results = parse_project(root, max_modules=0)
    except Exception as exc:
        return {"error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc)[:60]}"}
    rows = classify_variants(compute_duplicates(modules, results))
    cochange = git_cochange(root, keep_paths=frozenset(str(m.path) for m in modules))
    if cochange is None:
        return {"error": "not a git repo / git unavailable"}
    demoted = demote_independent(rows, counts=cochange.counts, pair_support=cochange.pair_support)
    before = sum(1 for g in rows if g.category == "duplicate")
    after = sum(1 for g in demoted if g.category == "duplicate")
    indep = [g for g in demoted if g.category == "variant" and g.variant_reason == "independent"]
    # A demotion is "source" if every member file is non-test (the highest-value
    # demotion - real parallel source implementations, not leaked test code).
    src_indep = sum(1 for g in indep if not any(is_test_path(m.path) for m in g.members))
    return {
        "primary_before": before,
        "primary_after": after,
        "demoted": len(indep),
        "demoted_source": src_indep,
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--stdout", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

class DuplicateMember(BaseModel):
    """One function participating in a duplicate cluster.

    `module` is the module qualname (the `parse_results` key); `qualified_name`
    is the in-module dotted name (e.g. `Foo.bar`); `path` + `line` give the
    file:line citation.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    module: str
    qualified_name: str

def classify_variants(groups: list[DuplicateGroup]) -> list[DuplicateGroup]:
    """Finalize each group's `category` / `variant_reason` from member source.

    Demotes likely-intentional clusters (issue #242) to the `"variant"` tier:
    `@overload` stubs, trivial `@property` shims, pure-boilerplate bodies, and
    same-class sibling methods. Reads each member file at most once; a member
    whose file cannot be read is treated as featureless (its signals abstain).
    """
    features_by_path: dict[str, dict[int, FunctionFeatures]] = {}

    def features_for(path: str) -> dict[int, FunctionFeatures]:
        return _read_cached(features_by_path, path, extract_function_features)

    classified: list[DuplicateGroup] = []
    for group in groups:
        feats = [features_for(m.path).get(m.line) for m in group.members]
        reason = _variant_reason(group, feats)
        classified.append(
            group.model_copy(
                update={
                    "variant_reason": reason,
                    "category": "variant" if reason is not None else "duplicate",
                    "exact": _is_exact(feats),
                }
            )
        )
    return classified


def _is_vendored_path(path: str) -> bool:
    """True when any path segment marks the file as vendored / isolation code."""
    return any(seg in _VENDOR_SEGMENTS for seg in Path(path).parts)


def is_test_path(path: str) -> bool:
    """True when the file is test code, by basename convention or a test dir.

    Public because change-coupling (#131) reuses it to default `archy coupling`
    to source-only (test co-change is mostly a test tracking the module it
    covers, which buries the source-to-source hidden coupling that matters).

    Parallel/legacy test suites produce byte-identical bodies by design (numpy's
    frozen `test_random.py` vs `test_randomstate.py`, per-module compliance
    scaffolding), so a cluster wholly inside test code is scaffolding, not a
    refactor target (issue #247, class 3).
    """
    p = Path(path)
    name = p.name
    if name == "conftest.py" or name.endswith("_test.py") or name.startswith("test_"):
        return True
    return any(seg in _TEST_DIR_SEGMENTS for seg in p.parts)


def _has_decorator(feat: FunctionFeatures | None, suffix: str) -> bool:
    return feat is not None and any(d.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] == suffix for d in feat.decorators)

    ddp._git(repo, "init", "-q")
    return repo


def _copy(name: str) -> str:
    return ddp._ORIGINAL.replace("summarize", name)


def test_added_line_ranges_parses_hunks_and_skips_deletions() -> None:
    diff = (
        "diff --git a/p/x.py b/p/x.py\n"
        "--- a/p/x.py\n"
        "+++ b/p/x.py\n"
        "@@ -3,0 +4,2 @@ def f():\n"
        "+a\n"
        "+b\n"
        "@@ -10,2 +11,0 @@\n"
        "-gone\n"
        "-gone\n"
        "@@ -20 +21 @@\n"
        "+one\n"
    )
    assert ddp.added_line_ranges(diff) == {"p/x.py": [(4, 5), (21, 21)]}


def test_copy_into_new_file_fires(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    repo = _repo(tmp_path)
    base = ddp._commit_fixture(repo, {"pkg/__init__.py": "", "pkg/a.py": ddp._ORIGINAL}, "base")
    head = ddp._commit_fixture(repo, {"pkg/b.py": _copy("summarise_again")}, "copy")

    out = ddp.analyze_checkout(repo, base, head)

    # The fixture must hold a pre-existing member: one member NOT in the diff.
    assert out["firings"], out
    members = out["firings"][0]["members"]
    assert [m["new"] for m in members].count(False) == 1
    assert [m["new"] for m in members].count(True) == 1


def test_two_new_copies_with_no_preexisting_member_do_not_fire(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Kills removal of condition B: both members are added, none existed at base."""
    repo = _repo(tmp_path)
    base = ddp._commit_fixture(repo, {"pkg/__init__.py": ""}, "base")
    head = ddp._commit_fixture(
        repo, {"pkg/a.py": _copy("one"), "pkg/b.py": _copy("two")}, "two new copies"
    )

    # Assert the fixture reaches the branch: the detector DOES cluster the pair.
    clusters = ddp.detect_clusters(repo)
    assert any(len(g.members) == 2 for g in clusters)

    assert ddp.analyze_checkout(repo, base, head)["firings"] == []


def test_backlog_cluster_untouched_by_the_diff_does_not_fire(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Kills removal of condition A: the pair is wholly at base and the PR adds an
    unrelated file, so no member's def line is inside an added hunk."""
    repo = _repo(tmp_path)
    base = ddp._commit_fixture(
        repo,
        {"pkg/__init__.py": "", "pkg/a.py": _copy("one"), "pkg/b.py": _copy("two")},
        "base with backlog duplicate",
    )
    head = ddp._commit_fixture(repo, {"pkg/c.py": "VALUE = 1\n"}, "unrelated addition")

    clusters = ddp.detect_clusters(repo)
    assert any(len(g.members) == 2 for g in clusters)  # the backlog cluster exists

    assert ddp.analyze_checkout(repo, base, head)["firings"] == []


def test_editing_an_existing_function_does_not_fire(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    repo = _repo(tmp_path)
    base = ddp._commit_fixture(repo, {"pkg/__init__.py": "", "pkg/a.py": ddp._ORIGINAL}, "base")
    head = ddp._commit_fixture(
        repo, {"pkg/a.py": ddp._ORIGINAL.replace('"big"', '"huge"')}, "edit only"
    )
    assert ddp.analyze_checkout(repo, base, head)["firings"] == []


def test_canary_passes() -> None:
    assert ddp.canary() == []

The full test suite is running in the background. I'll wait for it before committing.

Progress on the harness, on branch `alee/diff-duplicates-harness-548`:

- **Core:** `bench/diff_duplicates_precision.py` implements the preregistered firing rule. A cluster fires only if a member's `def` line is in an added hunk and another member is outside the added hunks. It runs the shipped detector unmodified: exact clusters with co-change demotion, plus near-miss at 0.85, source-only.
- **Canary:** `--canary` passes. A copy into a new file fires, and an edit-only PR doesn't.
- **Mutation checks:** I dropped each firing condition in turn, with `__pycache__` cleared. Dropping "member existed at base" turned `test_two_new_copies_with_no_preexisting_member_do_not_fire` red. Dropping "def line inside an added hunk" turned `test_backlog_cluster_untouched_by_the_diff_does_not_fire` red. In each case only the intended test failed, and the grep confirmed the mutation applied.
- **Gates:** `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty`, `archy check`, `archy cycles --strict` and `archy contracts` all pass. The derived headers were stale, so I regenerated them with `--write`. That touched `coupling.py`, `duplicates.py`, `graph.py` and `scan_config.py` (header blocks only).

One design point to flag: member paths from the detector are absolute, so a checkout under a `tests/` directory would mark every cluster as test code. I added a guard that drops such a checkout with a recorded reason instead of silently scoring it. The PR-sampling loop, the ledger and the pilot are not written yet, so `--canary` is the only mode for now.

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='bench/diff_duplicates_precision.py'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("def _source_only")
b=s.index("def detect_clusters")
new='''def _path_excluded(rel: str) -> bool:
    """Test or vendored path, judged on the path RELATIVE to the checkout."""
    return is_test_path(rel) or _is_vendored_path(rel)


def _source_only(groups: list[DuplicateGroup], root: Path) -> list[DuplicateGroup]:
    """Drop any cluster with ANY member in test or vendored code, as pre-registered.

    Stricter than the shipped `classify_variants`, which demotes only clusters lying
    WHOLLY in test or vendored code and keeps cross-tier ones (a source function that
    copies isolated code). The pre-registration drops those too, for exact and
    near-miss alike, so a cross-tier cluster never reaches the labelers.
    """
    return [g for g in groups if not any(_path_excluded(_rel(m.path, root)) for m in g.members)]


'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace("    near = _source_only(compute_near_duplicates(modules, parse_results, min_size=MIN_NODES))\n    return exact + near",
"    near = compute_near_duplicates(modules, parse_results, min_size=MIN_NODES)\n    return _source_only(exact + near, root)")
s=s.replace("    is_test_path,\n)","    _is_vendored_path,\n    is_test_path,\n)",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cat >> tests/test_diff_duplicates_precision.py <<'EOF'


def test_cross_tier_cluster_with_a_test_member_does_not_fire(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """The pre-registration drops a cluster with ANY test member, not only a wholly
    test one: a new source copy of a function that already lives in tests/ is out."""
    repo = _repo(tmp_path)
    base = ddp._commit_fixture(
        repo,
        {"pkg/__init__.py": "", "tests/helpers.py": _copy("one")},
        "base with a test-side function",
    )
    head = ddp._commit_fixture(repo, {"pkg/b.py": _copy("two")}, "source copy")

    # The shipped detector keeps this cluster (cross-tier stays primary) and the
    # diff makes it a firing by A and B, so only the path filter can stop it.
    raw = ddp.compute_duplicates(*ddp.parse_project(repo), min_size=ddp.MIN_NODES)
    assert any(len(g.members) == 2 for g in raw)

    assert ddp.analyze_checkout(repo, base, head)["firings"] == []
EOF

A new test covers a cross-tier cluster, and removing the filter turns that test red. The canary, `ruff`, `ty`, the `archy` gates and the duplicates tests all pass.

All other round-one reviews passed. That includes the structural check, which found only header edits in `coupling.py`, `duplicates.py`, `graph.py` and `scan_config.py`.

I've started a second review round on just the two files I changed. After it finishes I'll check CodeScene on #948 and report back.

"""PR sampling and checkout for the #548 harness (see `diff_duplicates_precision.py`).

The population, the seed and the per-repo cap are pre-registered in
`docs/research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md`; this module only implements them.

Pool: AIDev `pull_request` rows that are CLOSED (merged or closed-unmerged, never
open) in repositories whose AIDev `language` is Python. The repository language is a
sampling proxy only: whether a PR is a "Python PR" is decided from its own diff at
analysis time, and a PR with no added `.py` line is dropped (recorded, excluded from
the denominator).

pyarrow is NOT an archy dependency. Run the sampling with
`uv run --with pyarrow python bench/diff_duplicates_precision.py ...`.

archy:owns        PoolPR, Resolved, Unresolvable, draw_main, draw_pilot, load_pool, resolve
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
import subprocess
import urllib.request
from collections.abc import Iterator
from itertools import islice
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

SEED = 548
PILOT_N = 20
REPO_CAP = 25
AIDEV_URL = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hao-li/AIDev/resolve/main/"
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CACHE = REPO_ROOT / "bench" / "cache" / "aidev"
CLONES = Path("/tmp/archy_bench/aidev")
GIT_TIMEOUT = 900


class PoolPR(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    id: int
    number: int
    repo: str
    agent: str
    merged: bool


class Resolved(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    repo_dir: Path
    base: str
    head: str


class Unresolvable(Exception):
    """The PR cannot be reproduced for a reason that will not change on retry
    (deleted repository, pull ref gone). Recorded as a drop. Any OTHER failure is
    transient and the unit is retried, never dropped."""


def _download(name: str) -> Path:
    dest = CACHE / name
    if not dest.exists():
        CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        part = dest.with_suffix(dest.suffix + ".part")
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(AIDEV_URL + name, part)
        part.rename(dest)
    return dest


def load_pool() -> list[PoolPR]:
    """The closed-PR pool in Python-language repositories, sorted by AIDev id."""
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq  # ty: ignore[unresolved-import]  (optional, see module doc)

    repos = pq.read_table(_download("repository.parquet")).to_pylist()
    python_repos = {r["id"]: r["full_name"] for r in repos if r["language"] == "Python"}
    cols = ["id", "number", "agent", "state", "merged_at", "repo_id"]
    rows = pq.read_table(_download("pull_request.parquet"), columns=cols).to_pylist()
    pool = [
        PoolPR(
            id=r["id"],
            number=r["number"],
            repo=python_repos[r["repo_id"]],
            agent=r["agent"],
            merged=bool(r["merged_at"]),
        )
        for r in rows
        if r["repo_id"] in python_repos and r["state"] == "closed"
    ]
    return sorted(pool, key=lambda p: p.id)


def _shuffled(pool: list[PoolPR], seed: int) -> list[PoolPR]:
    ordered = sorted(pool, key=lambda p: p.id)
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(ordered)
    return ordered


def draw_pilot(pool: list[PoolPR], *, seed: int = SEED, n: int = PILOT_N) -> list[PoolPR]:
    """The first `n` of the seeded shuffle. The main sample never contains these."""
    return _shuffled(pool, seed)[:n]


def draw_main(
    pool: list[PoolPR], n: int, *, seed: int = SEED, pilot_n: int = PILOT_N, cap: int = REPO_CAP
) -> list[PoolPR]:
    """`n` PRs from the same shuffle AFTER the pilot, at most `cap` per repository,
    the cap applied in draw order (so the first `cap` PRs a repository reaches win)."""
    return list(islice(_main_stream(pool, seed, pilot_n, cap), n))


def _main_stream(pool: list[PoolPR], seed: int, pilot_n: int, cap: int) -> Iterator[PoolPR]:
    taken: dict[str, int] = {}
    for pr in _shuffled(pool, seed)[pilot_n:]:
        if taken.get(pr.repo, 0) >= cap:
            continue
        taken[pr.repo] = taken.get(pr.repo, 0) + 1
        yield pr


def _run(*cmd: str, cwd: Path | None = None) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT
    ).stdout


def _pr_shas(pr: PoolPR) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """`(base_sha, head_sha)` from the GitHub REST API (never GraphQL)."""
    try:
        raw = _run("gh", "api", f"repos/{pr.repo}/pulls/{pr.number}")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
        if "404" in (exc.stderr or ""):
            raise Unresolvable(f"pull request not found: {pr.repo}#{pr.number}") from exc
        raise
    data = json.loads(raw)
    return data["base"]["sha"], data["head"]["sha"]


def resolve(pr: PoolPR) -> Resolved:
    """Blobless-clone the repository (cached), fetch the PR's pull ref, and return
    `merge-base(base, head)` as the diff base, i.e. the three-dot diff GitHub shows."""
    base_sha, head_sha = _pr_shas(pr)
    repo_dir = CLONES / pr.repo.replace("/", "__")
    if not repo_dir.exists():
        CLONES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            _run(
                "git",
                "clone",
                "--quiet",
                "--filter=blob:none",
                "--no-checkout",
                f"https://github.com/{pr.repo}.git",
                str(repo_dir),
            )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
            if "not found" in (exc.stderr or "").lower():
                raise Unresolvable(f"repository gone: {pr.repo}") from exc
            raise
    try:
        _run("git", "fetch", "--quiet", "origin", f"pull/{pr.number}/head", cwd=repo_dir)
        head = _run("git", "rev-parse", "FETCH_HEAD", cwd=repo_dir).strip()
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
        if "couldn't find remote ref" in (exc.stderr or ""):
            raise Unresolvable(f"pull ref gone: {pr.repo}#{pr.number}") from exc
        raise
    base = _run("git", "merge-base", base_sha, head, cwd=repo_dir).strip()
    return Resolved(repo_dir=repo_dir, base=base, head=head or head_sha)

    cols = ["id", "number", "agent", "state", "merged_at", "repo_id"]
    rows = pq.read_table(_download("pull_request.parquet"), columns=cols).to_pylist()
    pool = [
        PoolPR(
            id=r["id"],
            number=r["number"],
            repo=python_repos[r["repo_id"]],
            agent=r["agent"],
            merged=bool(r["merged_at"]),
        )
        for r in rows
        if r["repo_id"] in python_repos and r["state"] == "closed"
    ]
    return sorted(pool, key=lambda p: p.id)


def _shuffled(pool: list[PoolPR], seed: int) -> list[PoolPR]:
    ordered = sorted(pool, key=lambda p: p.id)
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(ordered)
    return ordered


def draw_pilot(pool: list[PoolPR], *, seed: int = SEED, n: int = PILOT_N) -> list[PoolPR]:
    """The first `n` of the seeded shuffle. The main sample never contains these."""
    return _shuffled(pool, seed)[:n]


def draw_main(
    pool: list[PoolPR], n: int, *, seed: int = SEED, pilot_n: int = PILOT_N, cap: int = REPO_CAP
) -> list[PoolPR]:
    """`n` PRs from the same shuffle AFTER the pilot, at most `cap` per repository,
    the cap applied in draw order (so the first `cap` PRs a repository reaches win)."""
    return list(islice(_main_stream(pool, seed, pilot_n, cap), n))


def _main_stream(pool: list[PoolPR], seed: int, pilot_n: int, cap: int) -> Iterator[PoolPR]:
    taken: dict[str, int] = {}
    for pr in _shuffled(pool, seed)[pilot_n:]:
        if taken.get(pr.repo, 0) >= cap:
            continue
        taken[pr.repo] = taken.get(pr.repo, 0) + 1
        yield pr


def _run(*cmd: str, cwd: Path | None = None) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT
    ).stdout


def _pr_shas(pr: PoolPR) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """`(base_sha, head_sha)` from the GitHub REST API (never GraphQL)."""
    try:
        raw = _run("gh", "api", f"repos/{pr.repo}/pulls/{pr.number}")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
        if "404" in (exc.stderr or ""):
            raise Unresolvable(f"pull request not found: {pr.repo}#{pr.number}") from exc
        raise
    data = json.loads(raw)
    return data["base"]["sha"], data["head"]["sha"]


def resolve(pr: PoolPR) -> Resolved:
    """Blobless-clone the repository (cached), fetch the PR's pull ref, and return
    `merge-base(base, head)` as the diff base, i.e. the three-dot diff GitHub shows."""
    base_sha, head_sha = _pr_shas(pr)
    repo_dir = CLONES / pr.repo.replace("/", "__")
    if not repo_dir.exists():
        CLONES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            _run(
                "git",
                "clone",
                "--quiet",
                "--filter=blob:none",
                "--no-checkout",
                f"https://github.com/{pr.repo}.git",
                str(repo_dir),
            )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
            if "not found" in (exc.stderr or "").lower():
                raise Unresolvable(f"repository gone: {pr.repo}") from exc
            raise
    try:
        _run("git", "fetch", "--quiet", "origin", f"pull/{pr.number}/head", cwd=repo_dir)
        head = _run("git", "rev-parse", "FETCH_HEAD", cwd=repo_dir).strip()
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
        if "couldn't find remote ref" in (exc.stderr or ""):
            raise Unresolvable(f"pull ref gone: {pr.repo}#{pr.number}") from exc
        raise
    base = _run("git", "merge-base", base_sha, head, cwd=repo_dir).strip()
    return Resolved(repo_dir=repo_dir, base=base, head=head or head_sha)
